Purple Team Methodology.description: Purple team detection validation — run offensive TTPs, confirm SIEM/EDR fired, tune gaps. Collaborative red and blue team exercise.

steps.task: Define exercise scope and objectives — which attack scenarios to test?
Select TTPs from MITRE ATT&CK based on realistic threat actors targeting your industry
Agree on exercise environment — prod vs. dedicated test environment
Ensure blue team has baseline visibility before starting (confirm logging is working)
Set up tracking spreadsheet: TTP | Test date | Expected alert | Result | Tuning needed
Agree on communication cadence between red and blue during exercise
Verify all log sources are ingesting correctly — Sysmon, EDR, firewall, proxy, DNS
Map existing SIEM detection rules to MITRE ATT&CK — what do you already cover?
Identify ATT&CK coverage gaps — which techniques have no detection rule?
Prioritize gaps by likelihood of use by relevant threat actors (use ATT&CK Navigator)
Document detection coverage heatmap before exercise for comparison after
Execute TTP in test environment — document exact command/tool/timing used
Wait for detection window (typically 5-15 min depending on SIEM ingestion lag)
Blue team: check if alert fired in SIEM for this TTP
Blue team: check if EDR raised an alert for this TTP
If detected — verify alert quality: is the info actionable? Low false positive risk?
If NOT detected — identify which log source would catch it and whether it's available
Write detection rule if missing, test rule against execution artifact
Document result: Detected / Not Detected / Partially Detected / Logged but No Alert

Prioritize gaps by severity — which undetected TTPs are most dangerous?
Write new SIEM detection rules for each gap identified
Identify missing log sources — request deployment of Sysmon, DNS debug, etc.
Re-test every detection rule written during the exercise to confirm it works
Update ATT&CK Navigator coverage map after remediation
Produce detection coverage scorecard — before vs. after exercise
Document every TTP tested, result, and remediation action
Present findings to security leadership — focus on business risk from gaps
Schedule follow-up exercise to retest previous gaps and test new TTPs
